profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the easternmost row of the campus, the northern of two buildings arranged along that row. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet, plausibly this easternmost pair of buildings given how recently they appear to have been added to the campus footprint, though that specific match could not be confirmed. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from campus-wide totals.

reading.body:
Compass Datacenters operates Red Oak, a wholesale campus near Dallas-Fort Worth in Ellis County, Texas, where this building sits as the northern structure in the easternmost row of what the company describes as a 360 megawatt development. The operator's April 2024 expansion announcement added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet, which may correspond to this easternmost pair, though that match is not confirmed in available sources. No per-building capacity, tenant list, or completion date is published, so the power intensity of this specific structure cannot be stated.

The Red Oak campus is one of eleven mapped building footprints in this Compass cluster and represents the Dallas-Fort Worth market segment of Compass's broader portfolio, which also includes active sites in Chicago, Northern Virginia, Toronto, and Milan. Texas as a state has 133 mapped data center facilities, of which 18 publish capacity figures totaling 468 megawatts. This campus does not appear in the statewide published MW ranking because no single confirmed figure was available to assign to it.

Any reading of this site's relevance to AI scaling depends on data the operator has not yet released. The campus is real, the developer is established, and the expansion was recent enough to suggest active buildout. Until per-building specifications are published, the power available to tenants in this row and the timeline to operation remain unknown to this registry.
